name: Adverse Event Intake
one_liner: Multi-channel adverse event and product complaint capture with PV routing and SLA timers.
fits_when: adverse events and product complaints arrive by call centre, email, web form and field reps and must land in one queue
every report must be checked for the four minimum criteria before it counts as a valid case
duplicates across channels must be caught before PV spends time on a case
intake must route each case to pharmacovigilance within a fixed SLA, usually 24 hours from awareness
PV chases reporters for missing information with tracked follow-up attempts
cases are checked by QA and handed to a safety database, or worked by the PV team in the app
gives_you: A case record keyed by a case ID with channel, reporter, suspect product, patient, event and seriousness
A four minimum criteria check and a duplicate check before PV accepts the case
A routing SLA clock with at-risk and breached flags, and the 15 / 90-day regulatory due date
Events coded to MedDRA with seriousness criteria and outcome
Follow-up requests to reporters with due dates, attempts and responses
QA review against source documents, with an audit trail and a case 360 page

catalogue.description: One intake desk for every safety report. Intake agents log adverse events and product complaints from calls, email, web forms and field reps against the four minimum criteria; the duplicate check runs before a PV associate accepts the case within the routing SLA; PV codes the events, assesses seriousness and chases follow-ups; QA checks each case against its source documents before it is closed and exported to the safety database.

roles.name: Intake agent
roles.description: Logs reports from every channel, completes the minimum criteria and submits them to PV

roles.name: PV associate
roles.description: Clears duplicates, triages seriousness, codes events and requests follow-ups within the SLA

roles.name: QA reviewer
roles.description: Checks cases against source documents before export and investigates quality complaints

workflows.name: Multi-channel intake
workflows.description: Calls, email, web forms and field reps captured into one case record with its source documents

workflows.name: Duplicate check
workflows.description: Matching on product, patient and event flags likely duplicates before PV accepts a case

workflows.name: PV routing with SLA
workflows.description: A 24-hour routing clock with at-risk and breached flags, then the 15 / 90-day regulatory due date

workflows.name: Follow-up requests
workflows.description: Questions to the reporter with due dates, up to three attempts and recorded responses

compliance: PV SLA timers: 24 hours to route a case, 15 days for serious and 90 days for non-serious reports
Four minimum criteria check (identifiable patient, reporter, suspect product and event) before a case is valid
Source document retention with every case
Audit trail of every change and transition, aligned to GVP Module VI and 21 CFR Part 11 expectations
Patient identified only by initials, age and sex
